observations: body L1-L9: «al–Battānī» (L1) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.5 pt); the bar between «11° 50′» and «0° 37′ 21″» (L4) measures 9.8 pt, as long as the sign of equality, and is a minus sign. 41 years at al-Battānī's 54″ 33‴ a year (1° in 66 years) give 37′ 16″, and at the 54″ 28‴ of 11° 50′ in 782 years 37′ 13″; the printed 37′ 21″ and 11° 12′ 39″ are kept; either way the rounding gives 11° 13′.

body L10-L13: «Albateniana» and «al–Battānī» (L13) are letter-spaced, «al–Battānī» (L11) is not; their long dashes measure 5.3 (L11) and 5.5 pt (L13), and the minus sign of L13 9.4 pt. 41 years at Ptolemy's 36″ give 24′ 36″, the 25′ of L12.

body L14-L18: «al-Battānī» (L14) is letter-spaced, with a hyphen (3.2 pt), like «al-Battānī» in the head of the table (3.5 pt). The head of the table is set in a smaller type (x-height 4.7 pt, against 5.2 pt in the rows), the heads centred over their columns. The translation, p. 124, l. 23 and 29, gives β Scorpii at 5° 55′ Scorpii for Menelaus and at 17° 45′ Scorpii for al-Battānī: 17° 45′ − 5° 55′ = 11° 50′. Ptolemy's catalogue puts β Scorpii at 6° 1/3 Scorpii, Menelaus' 5° 55′ with Ptolemy's 25′ added, and 17° 45′ − 6° 20′ = 11° 25′, as printed in the last column; with the printed «6° 1/2» the difference would be 11° 15′. The printed «6° 1/2» is kept. For α Leonis, 14° 0′ − 2° 30′ = 11° 30′; the 11° 50′ from Menelaus is al-Battānī's common difference: with the 2° 40′ Leonis of the translation, p. 124, l. 24 (Plato 2° 22′), Regulus would have moved 11° 20′ to the 14° of l. 30.

body L19-L24: «Aṣ–Ṣūfī» (L19) is letter-spaced, «aṣ–Ṣūfī» (L23) is not; «Aṣ–Ṣūfī» and «Dhū ’l–qarnayn» have long dashes (5.3 pt each), and «42–» (L19) and «–43» (L20) the halves of a long dash broken at the end of the line (4.9 and 5.6 pt), as printed. The minus sign of L22 measures 10.2 pt, the dash before «Hinc» 9.7 pt. The year 1276 of the era of Dhū 'l-qarnayn, counted from 1 October 312 B.C., began on 1 October 964; 964 − 98 = 866; 866 years at 1° in 66 give 13° 7′ 16″; 13° 7′ − 0° 25′ = 12° 42′, which exceeds 11° 10′ by 1° 32′; 85 years (1191 to 1276 of the era) give 1° 17′.

body L25-L35: the dash after «II.» measures 9.8 pt; «Tycho Brahe» and «al–Battānī» (L26) are letter-spaced, the latter with a long dash (5.5 pt). Al-Battānī's obliquity of the ecliptic is 23° 35′; the ancients' 23° 51′ 20″ exceed it by 16′ 20″, about the quarter of a degree of Tycho. A speck before «prodat» (L28) is not transcribed.

body L36-L41: «al–Battānī» (L37) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.3 pt). The latitudes of Ptolemy's catalogue are in sixths and quarters of a degree, 10′, 15′, 20′, 30′, 40′, 45′ and 50′, as printed.

notes_left L1-L3: «al-Battānī» and «aṣ-Ṣūfī» are letter-spaced, with hyphens (3.1 and 4.0 pt). The interval of 40 years is that of the years 845 and 885 of Nabonassar (p. 292, note a, nr. I); «adn. b» stands for note a, the b being kept as printed.
notes_right L1-L3: one year's precession, 54″ 33‴, is the difference of 41 and 40 years.
